decision: Phase 9 technically and functionally closed on the validated Capture runtime. No further gameplay extraction is necessary for the Phase 9 gate; Phase 10 remains unopened.

publicEntry.meaning: Capture is classified as a first-class Shell module without historical Dungeon gameStyle; Shell activeModule remains capture throughout gameplay.

sessionAndHub.meaning: One Capture session/Hub entry and return owner; Save & Quit control is owner-local.

worldExploration.meaning: Physically extracted world/exploration runs and persists day 2, then day 3 after reload/resume without a prior Dungeon save.

teamAndBattle.meaning: 19 roster functions and 39 combat core functions have one physical Capture owner. Real Capture battle APIs resolve two victories (second after reload) with return to Capture world. UI/XP legacy inline code is not a foreign runtime activation.

saveAndResume.meaning: Fresh-profile no-Dungeon-state → world → victory → page close/recreate → resume → day advance → second battle/victory; save world and participants remain intact.

sessionShutdown.meaning: Two real Save & Quit cycles, clean root navigation and resume, hidden Capture hub/modals, no duplicate quit UI, zero pending owner-local animation frames. This does not assert universal teardown of dormant scripts.

noForeignRuntime.meaning: The exclusive active Shell module is Capture; no Dungeon runtime/state is created, Dungeon gameplay/skin stays inactive. Survival public entry contains pure wave-rule helpers, with no independent activated Survival module provider. Inert shared/legacy code may still be loaded.

deferredLegacyOwners: Capture battle action/UI functions currently remain in historical index.html; they use the existing Capture owner and do not activate Dungeon or Survival as hosts.
Capture XP/rewards and some options remain inline; defer purely physical extraction to later index.html lightening/ownership work (Phase 12), with independent tests and charter §26.
Possible dormant global code and broader app cleanup are out of Phase 9; no claim that all legacy scripts are physically unloaded.
